# Stoke

> Self-hosted control plane for agent traffic and the local, remote, or approved provider capacity you attach. Stoke authenticates and applies policy before dispatch; it does not ship a model catalogue or provider credits.

## Facts an agent needs before using it

- Default listen address: `127.0.0.1:8787`; config is TOML.
- Fail-closed: without `STOKE_API_KEYS` and without `STOKE_DEV=1`, every endpoint except `GET /health` rejects requests.
- OpenAI Chat Completions clients: `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`.
- Native Codex: `STOKE_API_KEY=... stoke run codex`; Stoke can read the existing native login at `~/.codex/auth.json` for the gateway-owned subscription path while `STOKE_API_KEYS` authenticates the gateway hop. Responses JSON, reasoning, tool calls, and SSE remain un-translated.
- Ollama: configure an `openai_compatible` provider at its loopback `/v1` endpoint; discover exact model IDs from `ollama list` or `/v1/nodes`.
- Hermes is one verified client. A Hermes custom provider can be named `codex_responses` with Responses wire and `key_env = "STOKE_API_KEY"`; keep Ollama on its separate `chat_completions` provider. See the [Hermes docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs) for the authoritative client schema.

## Release-scope behavior

- Cache identity is scoped to caller and named route and includes the resolved model plus the complete effective request. Cache policy is only for eligible non-streaming named routes; TTL reuse and lazy cleanup are not secure erasure. No Responses caching claim.
- Opt-in bounded exact coalescing can make identical cold eligible requests share one provider execution. Followers wait for a bounded interval and receipts remain dispatch-level.
- Validated `Retry-After` and `x-should-retry` values can be propagated to clients; this is not a new internal retry policy.
- Native Codex subscription auth may be gateway-owned from the existing `~/.codex/auth.json`; `STOKE_API_KEYS` remains gateway auth. Explicit separate client OAuth is supported. Subscription traffic bypasses per-token USD metering, but provider plan limits and Stoke rate/loop controls still apply.
- Optional Headroom is default-off and local. Before native Responses dispatch it accepts only a smaller, validated, lossless JSON-whitespace transformation for eligible tool-result strings; rejected or unavailable work retains the original outputs. The current worker lock targets macOS arm64 / CPython 3.11, with bounded request and batch sizes. It is not streamed-response compression or a universal token/billing-savings claim.

## Endpoints

- `GET /health` — liveness; only unauthenticated endpoint.
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` — OpenAI-compatible chat, SSE, and tool calls.
- `POST /v1/responses` — native OpenAI Responses JSON/SSE passthrough.
- `POST /v1/messages` — Anthropic Messages passthrough.
- `GET /v1/nodes` — protected live inventory, health, warm state, load, and latency.
- `GET /v1/budget`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/pricing`, `/v1/cache`, `/v1/routes` — protected status surfaces.

## Limits

Stable releases are tag-published; see https://github.com/Ozperium/stoke/releases/latest. No published performance, RTK, or general savings claim is made. Optional Headroom is default-off and limited to validated JSON tool-result whitespace compaction before native Responses dispatch; its current worker lock targets macOS arm64 / CPython 3.11. Local capacity costs electricity and hardware; subscription plans have no per-request USD price and cannot be dollar-capped by Stoke.
